findings.title: Task 2.2 omits the production BehavioralProfile construction site in migratory_server
findings.description: Description: Task 2.1 makes `leadership_weight` and `momentum_weight` required with no defaults, and task 2.2 ("Update all BehavioralProfile call sites in tests") restricts its update sweep to `tests/` ("search for `BehavioralProfile(` across `tests/`"). But `build_profiles()` in `src/migratory_server/simulation.py:18` constructs `BehavioralProfile` with only the 7 existing fields — a non-test source call site no task covers. That function is exercised by `tests/test_simulation.py` (the `build_profiles` tests at lines 29, 39, 45) and `tests/test_server.py` (`TestSimulationManagerIntegration`). After task 2.1, those tests will raise `TypeError`, making 2.2's verification gate ("all existing tests still pass") and 6.1's full-suite gate unattainable as written. This leaves the slice's technical requirement — "all affected tests are updated within this slice" (backward-incompatible update handled end-to-end) — unmet. The task file needs a step (or small task) in Section 2 to update `build_profiles`, and a decision on whether `ProfileConfig` in `src/migratory_server/config.py` gains the two fields (its optional-weight pattern at `_validate_profile` suggests that) or `build_profiles` passes explicit values — the latter being the choice consistent with the "never use silent fallback values" convention.

findings.title: "No nested Python loops" vectorization requirement is tracked by no task
findings.description: Description: The slice's Technical Requirements state: "Both forces are vectorized within each agent's neighborhood — no nested Python loops." No task in the breakdown restates or verifies this, and the task file contains no mention of vectorization anywhere. The risk is concrete: task 4.1 (LeadershipForce) is written in per-element index notation — `weighted_heading = sum(velocity[i] * leadership[i]) / sum(leadership)` — which a junior implementer can plausibly translate into a nested `for neighbor in neighbors` loop, and nothing in the verification steps (3.2, 4.2, 6.1, 6.2) would catch it, since no test observes loop structure. The established pattern in `src/migratory/engine/flocking.py` (single loop over agents, numpy operations within each neighborhood) is the intended one. One line added to tasks 3.1 and 4.1 — e.g. "follow the flocking.py pattern: one loop over agents, vectorized ops within the neighborhood; no per-neighbor Python loops" — closes the gap.

findings.title: Minor: 6.3 commit prefix may not match its content
findings.description:
Description: Task 6.3 says "Git add any remaining changes and commit: `docs: complete slice 102`". If "remaining changes" includes code (e.g., the `simulation.py` fix from the first finding landing late), the `docs:` prefix would misdescribe the commit against CLAUDE.md's semantic-commit rule. Informational — the implementer should re-check `git status` contents before choosing the prefix.

Verdict rationale: no FAIL — the plan is executable and its own verification gates would surface the `simulation.py` break quickly at task 2.2; the fix is small and local. The two gaps above should be patched into the task file before a junior AI starts work, hence CONCERNS rather than PASS.
